title: Ultra-Omni-Zeno Education
promise: Education is free for all who want to learn.
equation: LLL = Life Long Learning NAND Live Love Life

modules.title: The Free Door
modules.essential_question: What changes when learning is a commons rather than a commodity?
modules.promise: Start where you are. No application, no tuition, no permission.
practices: Write down the one thing you have been told you cannot learn.
Spend twenty minutes learning it from a free source.
Teach the first useful sentence back to someone.
modules.proof: A one-page learning charter: what you will learn, from whom, and who you will teach.

modules.title: The Live Classroom
modules.essential_question: What can a room full of beginners solve that a lone expert cannot?
modules.promise: Ask the unfinished question out loud. Confusion is shared infrastructure.
practices: Bring one question you are embarrassed not to know.
Answer someone else's question with a source, not an opinion.
Leave a written trace of what the room discovered.
modules.proof: One public question and one sourced answer, posted where the next learner can find them.

modules.title: The Sovereign Library
modules.essential_question: How do constraints make knowledge sharable across minds and machines?
modules.promise: Read the source, not only the summary. Attribution is an action.
practices: Pick one monograph or repository and read its abstract twice.
Trace one citation back to its origin.
Write a five-sentence summary that names what you do not understand.
modules.proof: A reading note with three links: the source, the citation, and your open question.

modules.title: The Measured Craft
modules.essential_question: What does it mean to know that something is actually faster?
modules.promise: A plausible branch may be ranked; only a verified branch may be bound.
practices: Choose one small function and state its contract.
Benchmark two implementations on your own machine.
Report the exact numbers and the conditions that produced them.
modules.proof: A benchmark note with code, cycle counts, architecture, and one honest caveat.

modules.title: The Open Forge
modules.essential_question: Who can learn from your work if it never leaves your laptop?
modules.promise: Publish small. Publish early. Keep it forkable.
practices: Create a repository with a README that states the problem.
Add a license and one runnable example.
Invite one correction by opening an issue on your own work.
modules.proof: A public repository with a README, a license, and one reproducible command.

modules.title: Techno-Buddhism
modules.essential_question: How do we build powerful systems without abandoning attention, honesty, and care?
modules.promise: Technology is not outside ethics. The loop includes the one who loops.
practices: Begin one work session with two minutes of silence and a clear intention.
Name one dependency your work has on other people and systems.
Stop when the work stops being honest; return when it is.
modules.proof: A short practice log: three sessions, what you noticed, what you changed.

modules.title: The Life Long Loop
modules.essential_question: What would you keep learning if no credential were waiting at the end?
modules.promise: The loop stays alive unless both learning and living have stopped.
practices: Choose one question to carry for a season.
Schedule a weekly lap with no performance target.
Teach one person one thing every week.
modules.proof: A living learning log with at least three laps and one thing you taught.
